items.title: Eddie Locke interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York, NY, January 13, 2001
items.q: And Roy Eldridge was the Godfather of my children, you know it was like my family you know. I had a great relationship with him

ctx.x: My name is Monk Rowe and I’m very pleased to have Eddie Locke here with me today in New York City for the Hamilton College Jazz Archive. I’ve been looking forward to talking to you because when I talk to people on the phone I get a certain vibe, and you seem like an interesting guy.

Well you know, the music business has been nice for me. Great. I always tell people, I said if I never played any more jazz, or if I never played any more music, my soul has been satisfied. Because I was very lucky. You know I played with Coleman Hawkins and Roy Eldridge. That is something, to be that lucky at the young age that I was. To play with one of them would have been good. But I played with both of them individually and I played with both of them together. It was like being fulfilled, jazz, music-wise,…
That really goes along with their legend, doesn’t it?
